ingrid: quick sync — i'm about to run a coordinated set of decode runs (replay harness vs synth) to compare kernel selection impact + batching heuristics for 7B and 13B. plan: lock tokenizer, seed, decoding params, and stop sequences. anyone object?
ajay: +1. can you list the exact params you'll lock? last time we had a tiny mismatch on stop tokens that skewed p50.
ingrid: good call. locking: `seed=42`, `temp=0.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_new_tokens=128`, stop=["\n\n"]; tokenizer: `hf/llama-tokenizer-v2` with `add_special_tokens=false`.
maria: also make sure KV cache warm vs cold is explicit. i want both cold-start (new session) and warmed (continuation). metricwise we need latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and kernel time breakouts (matmul vs softmax vs memcopy).
sam: for batching heuristics, run `dynamic_batcher` and `fixed_batcher` with batch sizes 1,4,8 and with `adaptive_timeout_ms` set to 0/5/20. include both streaming and non-streaming decode modes. small note: dynamic had been favoring larger GEMM kernels on 13B last run — check kernel overrides.
ingrid: noted. i'll add an explicit kernel override matrix: `--kernel-prefer=auto|sgemv_half|sgemm_fp16` to force different code paths. that will show where kernel selector is making the tradeoffs.
perf-bot: run queued: sync-decode-2165432100 by ingrid. expecting ~72 runs. i'll post artifacts when finished. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
nate: add profiling hooks: run `nsys` for end-to-end traces and `torch.profiler` (if torch path) to get operator breakdown. plz capture nvtx ranges around KV operations — those are the ones that hide memcopy overhead.
ajay: don't forget tokenizer alignment check: ensure `encode()` output length is identical between replay harness and synth harness for the same prompt. last time we had one-off due to line ending normalization.
maria: evaluation note: for apples-to-apples we should run the same stop sequences in both streaming and non-streaming modes — streaming can prematurely cut when using stop tokens if we don't buffer. make that explicit.
ingrid: will do. i'll also run a tiny perf regression probe: rerun a golden seed set from last stable commit and compare diffs. if we see >8% regression on p95 of latency or >10% token/sec drop, i'll block the kernel rollout.
sam: sounds good. can you capture system metrics (GPU temp, PCIe bw) alongside? sometimes noisy host IO masks real kernel perf.
ingrid: yes, nsys + dcgm exports. output path: https://redwood.internal/bench/2165432100-sync-decode (artifacts will include traces, csvs, and token-level logs).
perf-bot: first batch completed: 18/72. summary CSV uploaded.
ajay: one more: for the replay harness make sure we're not truncating prompts — run with `--preserve-prefix` and log prefix-len.
ingrid: will set preserve-prefix. timeline: start runs now, expect full results by EOD. i'll post a short summary thread with p95 deltas and any kernel-selection anomalies. thanks all. :v:
